title: Effect of Light Spectrum on Plant Growth: A Comparative Analysis
authors: Jane Doe, John Smith, Advisor: Prof. Dr. Alan Turing
affiliations:
Department of Applied Botany and Computing
Federal Research Institute

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
Controlled illumination in agricultural greenhouses optimizes the growth cycle of high-demand crop species.

This study investigates the impact of specific LED spectra compared with natural sunlight baseline on photosynthetic efficiency.

sections.title: Methodology
sections.content:
- Group A: Red and Blue LED mix (4:1 ratio).
- Group B: Standard filtered natural sunlight.
- Daily monitoring of dry biomass and leaf area over 60 days using automated IoT sensors.

sections.title: Results and Discussion
sections.content:
The targeted spectrum cohort (LED 4:1) achieved **32% higher** dry biomass accumulation compared to the control group, along with superior chlorophyll density.

Temporal growth variance was substantially reduced under continuous stabilized lighting regimes.

sections.title: Conclusions
sections.content: Targeted narrow-band LED spectra provide an energy-efficient, scalable cultivation strategy for modern urban and vertical greenhouse installations.
